deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §1 of Riemann's Göttingen doctoral dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The previous page argues that for a real variable, an 'arbitrary' dependence and one given by 'Grössenoperationen' (analytic expressions) amount to the same thing for continuous functions, because of Fourier/Dirichlet-type representation theorems. It then says this changes when z = x+yi is complex. Two infinitely close values z and z+dz, with dz = dx+dy i, correspond to w = u+vi and w+dw, with dw = du+dv i.

This page:
(1) Riemann claims that if w depends on z arbitrarily, the ratio (du+dv i)/(dx+dy i) generally varies with dx and dy, i.e. with the direction of dz. To show this he expands. (Steps marked [mine] are filled in by me.)
- [mine] du = u_x dx + u_y dy and dv = v_x dx + v_y dy.
- [mine] Hence du + i dv = (u_x + i v_x) dx + (u_y + i v_y) dy.
- [mine] Substitute dx = (dz + dz̄)/2 and dy = (dz − dz̄)/(2i), where dz̄ = dx − dy i.
- This gives
  dw/dz = ½[(u_x+v_y) + i(v_x−u_y)] + ½[(u_x−v_y) + i(v_x+u_y)]·(dx−dy i)/(dx+dy i).
- Writing dx+dy i = ε e^{iφ}, the factor (dx−dy i)/(dx+dy i) equals e^{−2iφ}. So
  dw/dz = ½[(u_x+v_y) + i(v_x−u_y)] + ½[(u_x−v_y) + i(v_x+u_y)] e^{−2iφ}.
- In modern Wirtinger notation this reads dw/dz = ∂w/∂z + (∂w/∂z̄) e^{−2iφ}. The quotient is independent of the direction φ exactly when ∂w/∂z̄ = 0, i.e. u_x = v_y and u_y = −v_x (the Cauchy–Riemann equations). Riemann derives these explicitly later in the dissertation, not on this page.

(2) He asserts that however w is built from z by combining the elementary operations of magnitude, dw/dz is independent of the particular value of dz. A footnote says this is easy to verify in each single case, but a strictly general proof would need a closer look at all the methods of defining one quantity as a function of another, which the purpose of the work does not require.

(3) It follows that not every arbitrary dependence of complex w on complex z can be expressed by such operations.

(4) The page begins to turn this property into a definition. The next page completes it: a function of a complex variable is any w whose dw/dz is independent of dz. That page also adds a draft footnote criticising Cauchy's notion of 'function' (Paris Academy session of 31 March).
errors: No mathematical error. The decomposition into dz and dz̄ coefficients and the identity (dx−dy i)/(dx+dy i) = e^{−2iφ} are correct.

The footnoted claim that every function built from 'Grössenoperationen' has a direction-independent derivative is heuristic. Riemann explicitly admits it is not proved in general and serves only as motivation. It tacitly assumes differentiability of u and v.

results.what: Decomposition of the difference quotient dw/dz into a direction-independent part plus a part times e^{−2iφ}; direction independence holds iff the second coefficient vanishes.
results.modern_name: Wirtinger derivatives ∂w/∂z, ∂w/∂z̄; dw/dz = w_z + w_z̄ e^{−2iφ}; Cauchy–Riemann condition w_z̄ = 0
results.usually_credited_to: Formula appears in Riemann's dissertation (1851); the operators were formalised by Wirtinger (1927); the Cauchy–Riemann equations go back to d'Alembert, Euler and Cauchy

results.what: Definition of a complex function (analytic function) as one whose derivative is independent of the direction of dz, motivated by functions given by analytic expressions.
results.modern_name: Complex differentiability / holomorphy as the definition of an analytic function (Riemann's 'geometric' approach)

deep.surprise_reason: This is essentially the text of §1 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation, with the same formula and argument. Only minor draft-wording variants (and, on the next page, a Cauchy footnote) could interest historians; the mathematics is well known as Riemann's.

checkable.sympy: ux,uy,vx,vy,dx,dy=symbols('ux uy vx vy dx dy',real=True); lhs=((ux*dx+uy*dy)+I*(vx*dx+vy*dy))/(dx+I*dy); rhs=Rational(1,2)*(ux+vy)+Rational(1,2)*(vx-uy)*I+Rational(1,2)*((ux-vy)+(vx+uy)*I)*(dx-I*dy)/(dx+I*dy); simplify(lhs-rhs)==0
checkable.asserts: Riemann's first equality for (du+dv i)/(dx+dy i)
(dx−dy i)/(dx+dy i) = e^{−2φi} when dx+dy i = ε e^{φi}
For a function built by operations (z^3) the direction-dependent coefficient vanishes

transcription_corrections: 'Das eben hervorgehobene Kennzeichen' should read 'Die eben hervorgehobene Eigenschaft' (the image shows 'Eigenschaft').
'compl[?]exen' is 'comple-xen' (complexen), hyphenated across the line break.
The numerator of the last fraction in the first formula line is 'dx−dy i' (the stroke looks like '∘' in places but means minus).
